trigger: standard user B replaces his offline <profile>\NTUSER.DAT with a hard link to another unloaded hive file owned by SYSTEM, Administrators or B (e.g. C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT); an operator then runs set_user_value or delete_user_value for B while B is logged off
classification_rationale: the routed security-posture registry row clause (4) and the software-estate privacy_permissions row (6) present the default-on hive-file guard as confining the offline arm; LeafFacts (win_hive_file_guard.hpp:163-170) carries no link count and classify_hive_file (:120-134) checks hard links for sidecars only, so a hard-linked leaf passes owner, final-path and after_load FileId checks
summary: Gate 7 B1 (derived CRITICAL: I1 base HIGH, E2 raises one band). Synthesiser verified the code gap: LeafFacts has no links field; Win32HiveFileProbe::leaf_facts (win_hive_file_probe.hpp:155) already calls GetFileInformationByHandle but drops nNumberOfLinks; only sidecar_facts (:223-224) reads it. Before 2.1.0 the offline arm only read; do_user_write (registry_win.cpp:665-712) now writes through it as SYSTEM with SeRestore. Trigger feasibility (can a standard user hard-link a hive file he cannot write) is UNVERIFIED: flagged for adjudication, kingsley falsifier = CreateHardLinkW as a standard user to C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT; if refused for every hive file B cannot write, E6 applies and the band caps at LOW. Fix (one guard, all consumers): add std::uint32_t links to LeafFacts filled at win_hive_file_probe.hpp:155, add a leaf_hardlinked fact set in before_load, refuse it after is_reparse in classify_hive_file with a new kHiveHardlinked token, fake-probe test in tests/unit/test_privacy_permissions_win_walk.cpp plus an ordering case in test_privacy_permissions_parsers.cpp; docs: the guard check lists in agents/plugins/privacy_permissions/README.md, the registry README per-user caveat, and the software-estate routed row (6) leaf list. The fix touches agents/shared/win_hive_file_guard.hpp, which re-triggers security-guardian + cpp-safety at Gate 8.

trigger: a real apply whose run_apply throws (allocation failure) after item k>0 has mutated, or whose sink fails after the first audit line while later already-applied items' audit lines are still queued; also an agent death mid-plan
classification_rationale: cluster CS-1 (cpp-safety, I1) + A1 (architect, I6 MEDIUM), same defect at run_apply (registry_core.hpp:1139-1330) and do_apply (registry_win.cpp:729): every mutation happens before any line reaches the sink. The single actions keep 'no mutation without its audit line out first (or the fixed line)'; apply does not. I1 vs I6 is contested between the two reporters and needs an independent adjudicator; the cluster carries the max derived band
summary: Gate 7 B2, provisional cluster CS-1 + A1, independently: 2 of 8 (Gate 3 wave). Synthesiser verified the mechanism: run_apply accumulates every audit, item and undo row in ActionOutput.lines and returns only after the loop (registry_core.hpp:1151-1329); do_apply hands the finished output to emit (registry_win.cpp:729); an exception discards it and report_exception writes only the fixed op=apply ... key=- line; emit_lines (registry_core.hpp:1338-1354) answers error|exception on a sink failure after the first audit line and drops the rest. Deciding lines for the contest: audit-log.md:177 already documents rows lost 'when a stream drops after a mutation' and that an exception row 'does not say whether the write landed' (supports A1's I6); the undo manifest, the only copy of previous values, is lost with the output (both reporters). Fix preferred by both reporters: give run_apply a sink parameter (the Ctx shape emit_lines already uses) and write each item's audit line, item row and undo rows as the item concludes, stopping the plan on a sink failure; minimum if an independent adjudicator rules I6/MEDIUM: one sentence in README apply limits and the apply definition that rows and manifest arrive only on completion and an interrupted real run leaves neither. UP-4 is the same class on recursive delete_key (separate row).

trigger: an operator reads the secret-exposure disclosure to decide who can see registry secrets after 2.1.0
classification_rationale: I7 raised to HIGH: the omission conceals security-relevant behaviour (which surfaces carry registry values and who reads them); the enumerations exist and name set_value/delete_value only
summary: Gate 7 B3. Synthesiser verified: README.md:314 (Sensitivity) and :350, audit-log.md:177 bold block, enterprise-readiness register row (~:597) and the security-posture routed row clause (3) list only set_value/delete_value parameters and responses. Missing: (a) the apply reply's undo manifest returns previous values up to kCaptureValueCap 4,096 B per value and kCaptureTotalCap 512 KiB per reply to Response:Read holders for 90 days, 16x the 256-byte audit cap the 2026-10-20 owner acceptance describes; (b) the apply plan parameter and set_user_value value/data_hex sit unredacted in executions.parameter_values (never pruned); (c) the new audit rows (apply.*, per-user) carry old/new. Echo: compliance-officer CO-4 concurs (adds other users' hive values as personal data). Fix (docs-writer wording, security-guardian owns routed row clause (3)): extend each list to name apply (plan, item and undo rows) and the per-user actions, with the 4,096-byte and 512 KiB bounds; PR body states the owner acceptance is applied to these surfaces.

trigger: an apply set_value/delete_value item refused before its previous value is captured (item.invalid such as invalid_type/invalid_data/unrepresentable_name, or facts.open_error access_denied/key_is_link/root_level_create/concurrent_change) on a value that exists
classification_rationale: the item row cell 10 and the registry.write audit row assert old_state=absent for a value that was never read; the README undo table (README.md:36) maps absent -> delete_value
summary: Gate 7 B4. Synthesiser verified by reading: OldValue::state defaults to OldState::absent (registry_parsers.hpp:522); run_apply runs row.old = budgeted_old(...) and fill_old(au, facts.old) for every value op (registry_core.hpp:1256-1259) whether or not capture_old ran (it runs only when handle != nullptr, :1210-1213); fill_old renders old_state from the default (:888-890). The single actions leave old_state=- on a refusal. An unfiltered reverse plan turns a refused set_value K\v into delete_value K\v. Echo: chaos-injector CH-1 (c). Fix: render '-' for old_state/old_type/old_hex and skip fill_old unless capture ran (handle != nullptr && value_op), and leave the CO-1 count fields at '-' the same way; one test: a refused-before-capture item over an existing value shows '-' in the item row and the audit line. Closure fixture: CH-1 (c).

trigger: an apply real run deletes a leaf whose DACL is explicit or protected (a vendor secret key with Users removed), or a volatile leaf, and the operator replays the documented undo
classification_rationale: the undo manifest restores values only, while undo_complete=1 and the README undo table (README.md:39) present it as the way to undo a delete_key; I7 raised (security-relevant: the replay widens a protected key's ACL), I3 (undo_complete=1 reads as complete)
summary: Gate 7 B5. Synthesiser verified: undo rows carry name, type and hex only (render_undo_row at registry_core.hpp:1302); the plugin never reads a key security descriptor, class or volatility (no RegGetKeySecurity/GetSecurityInfo in registry_win.cpp); create_sub passes nullptr security attributes and REG_OPTION_NON_VOLATILE (registry_win.cpp:258-260), so a replayed create_key inherits the parent ACL, comes back persistent, and under a volatile parent fails ERROR_CHILD_MUST_BE_VOLATILE. Overlaps HP-2's third bullet (kept separate, same fold). Echo: CH-1 (a). Fix in this change: state in the undo table, the apply definition and the undo_complete description that only values are restored (owner, DACL/SACL, class and volatility are not), so undo_complete speaks for values only; optional: flag undo_complete=0 for a protected or explicit DACL or a volatile leaf. Full capture of the security descriptor is UP-1-SD (would-file).

trigger: one plan holds two value items on one key whose names differ only in non-ASCII case (delete_value K Ärger + set_value K ärger) and the manifest is replayed in item order
classification_rationale: parse_plan's dependent_items check compares value names after fold_ascii only (registry_plan.hpp:205-217); the non-ASCII caveat (README.md:555) covers keys only; I7 raised (conceals a data-loss risk), I2 on forward replay
summary: Gate 7 B6. Synthesiser verified the parser half: names[i] = fold_ascii(name) and the value-op clash test is keys[i]==keys[j] && names[i]==names[j] (registry_plan.hpp:207,217); Windows value-name case-insensitivity across non-ASCII is OS behaviour, not run here (likely). Item 1 captures item 0's result as its old value, so forward replay restores then deletes; the dry run also shows a different old value from the real run. Echo: CH-1 (b). Fix: extend the non-ASCII caveat to value names in README and the apply definition, and state 'replay the undo in reverse item order' (correct for any sequential manifest); optional: refuse dependent_items for two non-ASCII value names on one key. Closure fixture: CH-1 (b).

trigger: a real recursive delete_key over a tree with a subkey that grants LocalSystem read/enumerate but not DELETE (TrustedInstaller-owned), or one an EDR registry callback denies

FakeRegistry already enforces per-handle masks.
